name: HERON (superfluid helium)
summary: A historical Brown University R&D programme developed superfluid helium as a target for real-time measurements of low-energy solar neutrinos. Full-scale performance was studied in a detector design rather than measured in an operating solar observatory.
detection_principle: Solar neutrinos would scatter elastically from electrons in superfluid helium. Scintillation photons, drifting ionisation electrons and helium excitations would be detected by cryogenic calorimeter arrays above the liquid; coded-aperture imaging would reject gamma-ray backgrounds.
technologies: Cryogenic superfluid-helium scintillation, charge extraction and calorimetry

sites.name: Full-scale site not fixed
sites.location: Brown University R&D was carried out in Providence, Rhode Island; no full-scale underground observatory was constructed.

status.label: Historical R&D; full-detector status not established
status.evidence: The historical programme is documented by a final DOE R&D report and a subsequent design simulation; a full-scale operating HERON solar detector is not established.

timeline.event: Full detector simulation and projected solar-flux precision published.

collaboration.name: HERON (superfluid helium) Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected participants named in the cited project publications.

key_parameters.name: 2007 design helium target
key_parameters.value: 21.6 tonnes total, with an 8-tonne fiducial region

key_parameters.name: Operating temperature concept
key_parameters.value: Approximately 30–50 mK in the 2007 detector design

key_parameters.name: Simulated five-year precision
key_parameters.value: pp: ±1.68%; beryllium-7: ±2.97%; forecasts including specified systematics

results.summary: Laboratory work demonstrated key helium signal-production and detection processes, without observing a solar-neutrino flux.
Simulation quantified possible pp and beryllium-7 flux precision for a five-year design exposure.

science_scope: This historical solar-neutrino concept is distinct from the 2025 Hybrid Elevated Radio Observatory for Neutrinos. Forecast precisions from simulations are not measured solar-neutrino fluxes.
